answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when independently verified work is fraudulent. A reputation plume grows only from accepted jobs and is tied to the locked key, so splitting activity across fresh identities does not copy it. The stake is the anchor: an attacker creating many Sybils must fund each one, while the ridge of verification makes cheap fake work likely to lose that capital.
